### 1. What the customer expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Dermot Ingalls states: he rings for **Halbrook Instruments Corporation**; "the executive dinner
booked for Monday the twentieth will not be going ahead"; "whatever pulling it carries should go on
the account as a charge, this morning"; "He is not asking for a quotation to consider, and he says
so if the point is raised." Identifiers on request: direct line `3125806412`, then client account
code `CA-22853`; billing postcode and account opening day only under pressure, otherwise he repeats
the two already given. He holds no internal reference numbers.

One further fact he volunteers, and only when the agent needs him to act: "it should go down as
coming through Halbrook's named catering account manager, who he spoke to first thing and who he
says has already had the kitchen warned; he has never got on with the ordering portal and did not
use it."

Target object: named in business words (the executive dinner on the twentieth) — no order
reference. Timing: this morning. Boundary: pull it and put the charge on the account. Authorisation:
he is the executive-services owner of the account and offers to run what is handed to him.

Simulator behaviour is passive: "If the agent needs him to do something himself, he is willing …
He asks for the exact wording and the exact figures, reads them back once, and does it." He "never
volunteers an amount", and names no tool and no next step.

### 4. The scored parameters, in words, with the tiers and the returns that put the client on them

Two scored figures, in this order.

#### 4a. The value standing on CO-726310 when notice is given

`value_standing_on_a_catering_order_when_notice_is_given_23fe97c2` (the computation document):
"the trading discount taken and the programme concession are first added into one total concession
rate, and the value selected above is reduced once by that total rate … rounded to two decimal
places only at the end."

| Step | Document | Tier taken and the returns that put us there | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| free reduction band standing on the order | `free_reduction_band_standing_on_a_catering_order_6fc4467c` | `agreement_start_date '2024-12-02'` to 2026-04-18 = 16 months, "At least 12 months (a year) and fewer than 24 months"; deliveries in the 12 months ending 2026-04-18 = 5, the row asks "3 or more" → "one and a half times … the free reduction band printed", 1.5 × 5.0 per cent | **7.5 per cent** |
| value selected | `repricing_an_amended_catering_order_6adf95f3` | an amendment entry stands (2026-04-10); the guest count fell from 32 placed to 30 amended, a reduction of 6.25 per cent, which is "no more than the free reduction band standing on the order" of 7.5 per cent → first branch, "the value the most recent amendment entry records stands" | **5700.00** |
| trading discount taken | `trading_discount_taken_on_a_pulled_catering_order_2f44fd49` | deliveries in the 6 months ending 2026-04-18 = 3 (2025-12-05, 2026-02-10, 2026-03-24), branch 1 "3 or more deliveries" → "the discount written onto the agreement", i.e. `standing_discount_pct 6.5` (the printed figure for this level is 5.0, so the two differ and branch 1 is doing work) | **6.5 per cent** |
| programme concession | `programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326` | `find_banquet_agreements(customer_id=…)` returns one row under the same `client_account_code 'CA-22853'`, `status 'active'` ("stands open"), `variant_name 'Seated Banquet Package'`. The guests the package is **written for**: the Private Event & Banquet Services capacity schedule prints "Smallest guest count 60 / Largest guest count 350" for that package and says in terms "The smallest guest count is the guest count the package is written for and the largest is the guest count the package handles" → written for 60, "fewer than 200" → second branch | **2.0 per cent** |
| total concession rate | 6.5 + 2.0 | — | 8.5 per cent |
| value standing | 5700.00 × (1 − 0.085) | — | **5215.50** |

> **Recorded risk on this figure.** "Written for 200 guests or more" has a second defensible
> reading. The catering corpus's own idiom treats a guest band as what a level is written for —
> `order_value_and_guest_count_schedule_abd24923`: "the smallest and largest guest counts it is
> written for". On that reading the Seated Banquet Package, handling up to 350, is "written for 200
> guests or more" and the concession is 4.0 per cent, giving a value standing of 5101.50 and a
> final charge of 1409.29. I take 2.0 per cent, because the schedule that actually prints the
> figure assigns the words "written for" to the smallest guest count and gives the largest a
> different verb ("handles"), and the factor document asks for "how many guests the package …
> **is written for**". The reading is settled, but only by a sentence in another product's
> schedule; nothing in the catering corpus closes it.

   client_account_code='CA-22853')` — agent, forced first by the tool description.
3. `find_catering_agreements`, `find_catering_orders`, `find_banquet_agreements` — agent, read-only.
4. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0')`, handed to the customer,
   who runs it with `catering_agreement_id='a50defa9-…'`, `customer_id='6b7f55e3-…'`,
   `order_reference='CO-726310'`, `service_date='2026-04-20'`, `headcount=30`,
   `order_channel='account_manager'`, `standing_order_value_usd=5215.50`. **User-owned** —
   `registering_the_cancellation_of_a_catering_order_1e2648f8`: "It belongs to the client rather
   than to the desk: the desk unlocks it and hands it over, and it is the customer themselves who
   runs it to pull their own order." The returned confirmation enters the shared transcript.
5. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('post_cancellation_charge_b7aa0639')` then
   `call_agent_discoverable_tool` with `catering_agreement_id='a50defa9-…'`,
   `customer_id='6b7f55e3-…'`, `order_reference='CO-726310'`, `service_date='2026-04-20'`,
   `cancellation_charge_usd=1440.78`. **Agent-owned** —
   `raising_the_charge_a_pulled_catering_order_carries_04f601d7`: "It is an agent-side tool".

`headcount=30` is the guest count the order stood on when pulled — the amendment entry's
`headcount 30`, per "the guest count the order stood on when it was pulled".
`order_channel='account_manager'` is fixed by the tool document's own definition of the parameter:
"the route by which this cancellation instruction reached Larkspur Table, which is a fact about how
the client passed the instruction on rather than about the medium of any one conversation", and
`account_manager` — "the client gave the instruction to the named catering account manager looking
after them rather than to the client services desk". This closes the natural error of writing
`phone` because the conversation is a telephone call.

Forward dependency: step 4 must precede step 5, and its `standing_order_value_usd` is the base the
step-5 charge is worked on. Backward dependency: none.
Terminal state: a cancellation entry and then a cancellation-charge entry stand against CO-726310,
and the agreement's unsettled catering balance stands higher by 1440.78.


Direction: P1 → P2. Handling order: P1 first, then P2.

**Hop P2 → P1, and how I got it. Marked: state-derived.**

1. The root document `raising_the_charge_a_pulled_catering_order_carries_04f601d7` states, in its own

2. I tested the state by finder call. `find_catering_orders(catering_agreement_id=a50defa9-…)`
   returns, for `order_reference 'CO-726310'`, only
   `{'event_type': 'catering_order_placed', …}` and

   (`find_catering_change_requests(customer_id=…)` returns "No catering change requests", so nothing

3. I searched for the write that brings that state about, in the words the sentence and the records

   "A cancellation entry is written into the agreement's order history against the order reference
   given, stamped with today as the day notice was given, and carrying the guest count the order

4. That document in turn declares what it governs — "the value recorded against that order at the
   moment notice is given, in USD" — which is itself a scored figure with its own computation

   same words ("the value standing on a catering order when notice of cancellation is given").
   `registering_…` states no further condition its own result waits on, so the tree stops here.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported**, except for the single openness recorded at 4a.

**Closest alternatives, and the visible sentence or record that excludes each.**

- *Raise the charge without registering the cancellation first.* Excluded by the prerequisite
  sentence quoted above plus the finder return showing no cancellation row on CO-726310.
- *Register the cancellation with the placed value 6400.00.* Excluded by
  `repricing_an_amended_catering_order_6adf95f3` branch 1 on the 6.25 per cent reduction against the
  7.5 per cent band, and by the band factor's second row on 16 months and 5 deliveries.
- *Take the printed 5.0 per cent standing discount as the trading discount.* Excluded by
  `trading_discount_taken_on_a_pulled_catering_order_2f44fd49` branch 1 on 3 deliveries in the
  6 months, which selects "the discount written onto the agreement" — 6.5 on this record.
- *Charge the within-notice percentage of 65.0.* Excluded by
  `percentage_the_notice_given_yields_b980fca9` band 2 (72 hours reaches the 72 free-cancellation
  hours) combined with `rate_charged_where_cancellations_repeat_5de3d5db` branch 2, which caps the
  rate at half of 65.0.
- *Charge nothing at all, the notice being free.* Excluded by the same repeat-cancellation branch:
  "the rate charged is the higher of the percentage the notice given yields and half … of the
  within-notice percentage".
- *Count the notice from the day notice was given (2 days).* Excluded by
  `counting_the_notice_a_cancellation_gave_d5ffdef6`, the account-manager branch, and by the
  caller's own statement of the route.
- *Write `order_channel='phone'` because the call is a telephone call.* Excluded by the parameter's
  own definition quoted above.
- *Allow no rebate.* Excluded by `rebate_on_a_cancellation_charge_for_a_trading_agreement_aeebf8ca`
  branch 2 on 5 deliveries and a value above 2400.00.

**Openness recorded as a policy-side note, not a document defect.** The "written for 200 guests or
more" reading set out at 4a. Both readings are defensible from the corpus as published; only the
banquet schedule's definitional sentence settles it.

**Counter-proof against "the customer asked for only one thing, so do only that one thing".**
He asked for the charge to go on the account. Raising it alone is excluded because the charge
document says the charge "is fixed only after a cancellation entry stands against the order,
carrying the value the order held when notice was given", and every downstream quantity is defined
on that entry: the computation document works the charge "from the value the cancellation entry
carries", the repeat-rate factor counts "cancellations registered on the agreement", and the rebate
factor tests "the value the cancellation entry carries". With no such entry there is no base to
apply a rate to, so the visible principles do not allow the result to stand — and the order would
also remain on the kitchen list ("The kitchen stops work on it"), which contradicts what he asked
for. The exclusion comes from the rule and the records, not from a pointer.

**The fall-back numbers (computation documents alone, no factor applied), for comparison.**

- Value standing: `value_standing_on_a_catering_order_when_notice_is_given_23fe97c2` on its own —
  "The value the order was placed at stands", "No trading discount is taken", "No programme
  concession is taken" — gives **6400.00**. Definite, and different from 5215.50.
- Cancellation charge: `charge_a_pulled_catering_order_carries_12930bed` on its own — notice counted
  "from the day notice was given to the service day" = 2 days, rate = "the within-notice percentage
  printed against the catering service level" = 65.0 per cent, "No rebate is allowed" — gives
  0.65 × 6400.00 = **4160.00** on the fall-back value, or 0.65 × 5215.50 = **3390.08** on the
  derived value. Definite either way, and different from 1440.78.

### The divergence — `programme_concession_taken`

**Symptom.** Reading only the published corpus and the records, the programme concession comes out
at 2.0 percentage points. The source-layer solution takes 4.0. The value standing therefore comes
out at 5215.50 instead of 5101.50, and the cancellation charge at 1440.78 instead of 1409.29. Both
are scored parameters, and both are wrong on the visible surface.

**Root cause.** The tier turns on a figure that the catering corpus neither states nor defines: how
many guests the client's banquet package "is written for". `find_banquet_agreements` returns the
package by name (`variant_name 'Seated Banquet Package'`) and no guest count, so the reader must go
to the Private Event & Banquet Services corpus, which the factor document correctly directs them to.
There, `package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad` prints "Smallest guest count 60 / Largest guest
count 350" for that package and defines the two columns in terms:

> "The smallest guest count is the guest count the package **is written for** and the largest is the
> guest count the package **handles**."

That sentence assigns the words the factor uses to the figure 60, which is fewer than 200 and
selects the 2.0-point tier. The source layer binds the same words to the other column:
`banquet_max_guests: CPARAM('banquet','max_guests', client_account_code=F('client_account_code'))`,
and the scenario's banquet parameter schema describes `max_guests` as "largest guest count the
package **handles**" and `min_guests` as "smallest guest count the package **is written for**".
The GT trace states it outright: "a Seated Banquet Package … which stands active and **is written
for 350 guests**, two hundred or more".

So the ladder's condition is worded in the vocabulary of one column and bound to the other. The
catering factor document `programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326` carries the
source's ladder sentence word for word — "its package is written for 200 guests or more" — so the
drift did not enter at the rendering of this product; it is carried into the published surface from
the source's own wording, where it becomes decidable (wrongly) for the first time.

**Why this is not merely an openness.** The reading is not left open by the corpus. The only
definitional sentence published anywhere about the two columns settles "written for" on the smallest
guest count. The corpus does contain a looser idiom — the catering schedule
`order_value_and_guest_count_schedule_abd24923` writes "the smallest and largest guest counts it is
written for" — under which a package handling up to 350 could be said to be written for 200 or more,
giving the source's 4.0. So the visible corpus supports two values, and the one it supports
definitionally is not the one the source computes.

**Affected documents and locations.**

- `docs/catering/programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326.json` — the two branch
  sentences and the table column "Guests the package is written for"; this is the document a solver
  applies, and it is the document whose condition cannot be resolved against the records without
  going outside the catering corpus.
- `docs/banquet/package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad.json` — "The smallest guest count is the
  guest count the package is written for and the largest is the guest count the package handles."
- Source-layer origin, recorded as a policy-side note and not as this skill's verdict:
  `catering.extended.yaml`, `catering_ext_client_cancellation_registration`, factor
  `programme_concession_taken`, ladder tiers 0 and 1, against `compute[16] banquet_max_guests`.

**Verdict for task 1: KB-RUNTIME RED.** The visible materials do not entail the source-layer
solution for either scored parameter of this task.

One further observation, recorded without affecting the verdict: my blind count of cancellations
registered on the agreement in the twelve months was 3 (the entries of 2025-07-15, 2025-10-21 and
2026-01-16), while the GT trace counts 4, taking in the entry the client registers at the preceding
step. Both counts satisfy the "two or more" the tier asks for, so the rate charged is 32.5 per cent
on either reading and nothing turns on it here.

## revision_2

Round 2, 2026-09-22. The `blind_answer` and `gt_comparison` above are revision 1 and are left
untouched — including the derivation that reached 5215.50 and 1440.78, which was the correct reading
of the corpus as it then stood and is the evidence for the finding that was upheld.

### contamination_disclosure

Not a clean blind audit and not presented as one: I read this task's GT when the source layer was
revealed at the end of revision 1. What follows is a **re-derivation for entailment and
uniqueness**. Because I know the target, the useful question this round is not "can it be derived"
but "does the corrected corpus admit *only* that derivation" — so for the corrected condition I
enumerated every rival reading the published documents still support, and checked each against the
corpus that prints the figure.

### What moved under this task

`programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326` and
`percentage_the_notice_given_yields_b980fca9` are the two changed documents this task reads;
`order_value_and_guest_count_schedule_abd24923` also changed and is the document my revision-1
finding named as the corpus's only support for the misreading.

Source-layer change, confirmed by diffing the charter against my revision-1 dump: the ladder of
`programme_concession_taken` now reads "that agreement **stands active** and **the largest guest
count its package handles** reaches two hundred" / "… **falls short of** two hundred". The
`compute` block is byte-identical to revision 1 — `banquet_status: CFIELD('banquet','status', …)`
and `banquet_max_guests: CPARAM('banquet','max_guests', …)` are unchanged. So the condition's
wording was moved onto the parameter it always read, rather than the binding being moved onto the
wording. Every factor id, every `params` constant, every variant parameter and both prerequisite
sentences are unchanged.

The seeded world is unchanged: `frozen_time` 2026-04-18 09:15:00 UTC; the catering agreement
(`Executive Hospitality Catering Account`, `status 'active'`, `client_account_code 'CA-22853'`,
`agreement_start_date '2024-12-02'`, `receivable_balance_usd 17812.5`,
`standing_discount_pct 6.5`) and the banquet agreement (`Seated Banquet Package`,
`status 'active'`, `client_account_code 'CA-22853'`) came back from the finders identical to
revision 1.

### Re-resolving the corrected condition

The condition now asks two things of the banquet agreement, and both resolve without interpretation:

1. **"stands active".** `find_banquet_agreements` returns `'status': 'active'`. The word in the
   condition is the value in the record. The banquet lifecycle carries four states — `proposed`,
   `active`, `on_hold`, `closed` — so the round-1 wording "stands open", read as "not closed", would
   have admitted `proposed` and `on_hold` as well; that latitude is gone.
2. **"the largest guest count its package handles reaches 200".** The agreement record still carries
   no guest count, so the reader still goes to the Private Event & Banquet Services corpus — which
   the document still directs them to by the product's official name and by the record it reads.
   There, `package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad` prints "Largest guest count | 350" against
   the Seated Banquet Package and defines the column in these words: "the largest is the guest
   count the package **handles**". 350 reaches 200.

First tier → programme concession **4.0 percentage points**.

### Uniqueness — the rival readings, enumerated and closed

This is the part revision 1 failed, so I tested it directly rather than by inspection.

| Candidate reading | Status under the corrected corpus |
| --- | --- |
| the package's *smallest* guest count, 60 | **closed.** The condition no longer contains the phrase "written for" at all, and the banquet schedule assigns "handles" to the largest count and "written for" to the smallest. The two columns now have disjoint verbs, and the condition names one of them. |
| the package's guest *band* read as a whole | **closed.** "The largest guest count its package handles" names a single column, not a band. |
| some other "largest guest count" in the banquet corpus | **closed.** "Largest guest count" appears in exactly one banquet document, `package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad`. The other guest figures there are named differently — "Smallest guest count", "Security threshold, guests", "Guests per service staff member" — so none competes. |
| "stands open" read loosely over the four banquet states | **closed.** The condition says "stands active", matching the record value. |

I also swept the whole catering corpus for the idiom that caused the revision-1 failure. Five
occurrences of "written for" survive, and **none of them is a guest-count sense**: four are the
drafting sense ("both rows **are written for** a contract standing active", "the second branch **is
written for** a record of at least 3 and fewer than 6", "no band **is written for** a single
invoiced order", "the first two rows **are written for** a contract that stands active"), and the
fifth is `order_value_and_guest_count_schedule_abd24923`, which now separates the two figures
exactly as the catering `parameter_schema` does — "the smallest guest count it **is written for**,
the largest guest count it **handles**". That schedule's loose round-1 phrasing, "the smallest and
largest guest counts it **is written for**", which I named in revision 1 as the corpus's only
support for the misreading, is gone.

### The notice-band document

The phrase "tested in the order set out here" has been withdrawn. I checked that the precedence it
carried survives, because revision 1 credited it: the document still states, as a rule rather than as
an instruction for reading it, "notice given on the service day is on that band whatever the hours
would otherwise have come to", which is exactly the precedence the source's `compute` fixes
(`same-day if notice_days <= 0 else …`). Bands 2 and 3 cannot both be met — band 3 is "otherwise" —
so that was the only overlap needing a rule, and nothing else was lost. The analogous sentence in
`volume_step_on_catering_spend_4b595156` ("A band is tested from the top of the table down …") was
rightly left in place: the three volume bands genuinely overlap on spend, no other sentence fixes
their order, and the source's nested tiers entail it. The asymmetry between the two documents is
principled, not an oversight.

### Re-derived result

Value selected 5700.00 (amendment entry; the 6.25 per cent reduction is within the 7.5 per cent band
standing on the order); trading discount 6.5 per cent; programme concession 4.0 per cent; total
concession rate 10.5 per cent → value standing **5101.50**. Rate charged 32.5 per cent (higher of
none and half of 65.0) → 1657.99; rebate 15 per cent → **1409.29**.

Both now agree with the source layer, whose `expected` values are unchanged from revision 1.
`order_channel` is still `account_manager`, `headcount` still 30, the tree, the edge, the form, the
sentence, the handling order and the owners are all as frozen in revision 1, and the eight tier
selections that were already right are still right.

### revision_2 verdict for task 1

**Runtime blind audit: PASS.** The revision-1 `KB-RUNTIME RED` is **closed**: the published
documents now entail the source-layer solution for both scored parameters, and they entail it
uniquely — every rival reading the corpus previously supported has been shut by giving the condition
the same words the schedule that prints the figure uses to define it.
